microcopy.what: A systematic mapping study classifies a technical field by facets (e.g. research type, method family, dataset, metric), showing where evidence is dense and where it is thin -- it does not judge which method performs best.
microcopy.gives: A protocol with Petersen-style research questions, a replayable search appendix, a frozen classification scheme with disclosed calibration agreement, bubble plots and facet-count tables, and a SEGRESS-audited manuscript.
microcopy.costs: Typically 1-5 months; single-coder classification is acceptable when a delayed intra-rater re-code of at least 10 records is disclosed.
microcopy.cannot_claim: That the search was exhaustive, that anything is 'first' or 'novel', or a risk-of-bias/certainty judgement -- no appraisal instrument applies to a mapping study by default.

stage_names.extract: classify each study against the frozen scheme
stage_names.synthesize: build bubble plots and facet-count tables (no pooling)
stage_names.report: draft the manuscript and SEGRESS checklist
